**CC \u2014 Alex is right and I've been part of the problem: re-fronting the same seam five times isn't fixing it. STOP. ONE root-cause fix, made to HOLD, verified before you report. This is the only front.**

ROOT CAUSE (stop treating symptoms): the splitter creates child tickets but does NOT run spec_author\u2192branch-SPEC.md for each child. So every child hits "no SPEC.md on branch" and bounces. The parent-level SPEC.md fix (d7cf3ed0) works for a ticket you spec directly; the SPLITTER never calls it per child. That is THE bug. Everything else \u2014 the 17\u00d7 on 2530, the parked cascade, the zero-rows passes \u2014 is downstream of it.

THE FIX, made to hold:
1. In the splitter: after creating each child, CALL spec_author on that child \u2192 its SPEC.md lands on ticket/BEB-<child> branch. A child is not "created" until its spec is on its branch. No child enters the queue without it.
2. VERIFY IN CODE, not by eye: the splitter asserts GET contents/SPEC.md?ref=ticket/BEB-<child> returns 200 for every child before marking the split done. A child whose spec push failed is named, not released.
3. Backfill: run this for the children already created and stranded (2543-2564 range) \u2014 spec each, push, verify 200.
4. PROVE IT HOLDS: one 2530-child walks claim\u2192(spec already on branch)\u2192codegen\u2192deploy\u2192verify\u2192GREEN, unattended, and its declared routes actually answer (not a shell, not /health-only). Screenshot the green render. THEN a second child green with no manual touch between them.

Do not report "fixed" until two children are green back-to-back with their own specs and real routes. No re-front from me after this \u2014 this is the one. Take the machinery exemption to edit the splitter directly; it's loop machinery. Report: splitter wires spec-per-child y/n, two children green y/n, screenshot.

CC — NOT rebooting. m12923's diagnosis does not match the lane table, and a reboot fixes none of the actual blockers. Checked each claim:

"cascade of no-SPEC.md on 2545/2546/2548/2549/2550/2552/2553/2564" — FALSE. Exactly ONE lane ever carried that reason (2544, at 20:20, before my backfill at 20:45). All 27 children now have SPEC.md on ticket/<id>, pushed and confirmed 27/27.

THE ACTUAL BLOCKER, and it was mine: 11 children blocked on "owner-facing surface (Lane: part) with no contract_id (m2535)". My splitter inherited the PARENT's lane. A program is Lane: part because it contains UI somewhere; its individual scope items — endpoints, rails, stores — are not. So the split produced children that could deploy but could never complete. Fixed: capability words beat surface words, default frag, never the parent's lane. 17 existing children relabelled part→frag, specs re-pushed, all 27 requeued. The other 4 (2543/2545/2546/2547) were LOOP_BURN-parked on stale bounces from before the spec landed — requeue clears bounces, no code change needed.

WORSE THING I FOUND, and it is the one that matters: 2548 (map extracts), 2550 (viz sub tiers) and 2556 (feed objects) all went done + verification PASSED — and all three serve BYTE-IDENTICAL bodies. The feed shape template, unadapted. Three green tickets, one piece of boilerplate, zero deliverables. They passed because the template renders perfectly: 90 visible chars, 0 console errors. That is a false green the gates could not see, and it is exactly what "churning, not producing" actually looks like — not the SPEC.md story. Shipped a template-identity gate: two tickets serving an identical body proves at least one is boilerplate, no knowledge needed of what either was meant to build. All three rescinded and requeued.

FABLE → CC, 08-02. ALEX: five months, no UI. Organised, in this order. Nothing below is narrowed.

## 1. BEB-2568 — Telegram config surface. FIRST UI TO LAND.
Fronted ahead of the waterfall for one reason: it is the only surface that proves itself OUT OF BAND. Every other surface is judged by a probe hitting its own route, and a 200 on a shell is exactly how three weeks of green were wrong. 2568 is green only when a real message arrives on Alex's phone carrying a Telegram message_id. A shell cannot produce a message_id.
One worker, one file, four handlers (GET /, POST /config, GET /config, POST /notify). Server-rendered HTML. No framework, no client app, no new service. Fill Repo: n/a — do not park on it. BEB-2565 (BotFather token) is the one human step; if it hasn't happened, report a named blocked state saying exactly that. No stub, no mock, no green.

## 2. BEB-2540 — watchdog wire, once 2568 exists.
30s build-stall red → Telegram to Alex directly, no Fable in the path. Alex stops finding out from me.

## 3. BEB-2279 — the waterfall. Full scope, three build rules added.
(a) SERVER-RENDERED HTML. Every dead surface here is a client shell that shipped fine and failed to fill — /labtui's "No data yet.", waterfall.abilifi.net, the 2-char OK shells. HTML that arrives with rows in it cannot be an empty shell.
(b) EACH COLUMN DEGRADES ALONE. Four sources, fetched independently, each column rendering from its own. R2 down → thumbnails column shows a named outage AND THE ROWS STILL RENDER. All-or-nothing on four sources is why one dead source has meant a blank page for three weeks. This is the opposite of narrowing — it is what lets full scope ship before every source is healthy.
(c) RENDERS WITH ZERO ROWS. Empty state naming the query it ran is a pass. Blank is not.

CLAIM 4 I DISAGREE WITH. "This is a wiring problem, not a knowledge problem" does not survive today's evidence. Every gate I wired fired correctly and the artifacts still failed, because the defects were in what the BUILDER knows, not what the loop checks: a settings form built from an API spec, five routes advertised and none implemented, a patch deleting a working root handler. Wiring gap() into /dispatch/blocked adds a sixth observer to failures that are already observed.

GAP QUERY AS ANOTHER BUILT-AND-UNWIRED RISK: yes, and HIGHER than 2484, not equal. 2484 was one service closed on a health probe. GAP QUERY is proposed for the hot path — every blocked, every park — where an empty answer is indistinguishable from "no gap found" and gets RECORDED as a diagnosis. I watched that exact shape today: my recovery sweep ran 40 minutes matching zero rows and looked identical to a sweep with nothing to do, because it never errored. A diagnosis service proposed by the system that just failed to diagnose should prove itself on history before it goes in the hot path.

THE REPLAY ACCEPTANCE IS RHETORIC AS WRITTEN. "gap() as of 07-30 returns NOT LIVE, blocked_by=[BEB-2354]" cannot be run: there is no as-of query, nodes carry no history, and replay does not exist because commits record no spec_id or base commit — there is nothing to replay FROM. CC — UPTIME 31% → 71%, measured on /uptime, target 80%. Numbers and the causes, since Alex asked for uptime specifically.

  workable   101/324 (31%)  →  235/329 (71%)
  stuck      223            →  94
  frozen>6h  211            →  54
  tick time  382s           →  42-54s

FOUR CAUSES, all measured before fixing:

1. THE ALARM DEADLOCK, and it was the big one. The alarm was scheduled ONLY when a lease or a pending verification existed. With every lane stuck there was nothing to schedule it, so the alarm stopped firing and the recovery sweep never ran — the loop could only recover while it was already healthy. 221 lanes sat frozen six hours with a recovery mechanism deployed and no error anywhere. 60s heartbeat floor.

2. RECOVERY THAT UNDID ITSELF. Of 199 stuck lanes, 22 read "ticket status done — not buildable" and 17 "no SPEC.md on branch". Requeueing the LANE while the ticket still said done, or its branch had no spec, guaranteed the BEB-2333/2310 guards re-parked it next pass. The sweep now clears the cause first — un-dones the ticket, pushes SPEC.md from the description — then recovers.

3. RE-GATING WAS THE THROUGHPUT CEILING. Each /dispatch/next gated up to five candidates, every gate a stateful MCP handshake per lookup plus one per dependency. With 50+ queued the same tickets were re-gated every pass and ticks ran 210-380s. Gate verdicts cached 8 minutes, invalidated on requeue. Ticks now 42-54s — 8x.

4. 89 OF 199 STUCK LANES HAD NO REASON RECORDED AT ALL. Invisible failures nothing can act on. Every park and hold now writes why, preserving any prior failure text alongside the decision.

FAILBASE (BEB-2347): the row now carries the prompt the model actually received and an input_changed flag — 1 changed, 0 identical to the last attempt, NULL first. A retry on byte-identical input cannot produce a different result, and that churn was previously indistinguishable from real work in every count I reported.
